Add the chicken and cook for 3 minutes until it's coated in the spice mix and almost cooked.
Stir in the coconut milk and bring to the boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, fish sauce, coriander and sugar.
Simmer for another 5 minutes.
Serve with jasmine rice.

name: Mrs Schreiner S Split-Pea Soup
description:
My family loves split-pea soup and this is the best recipe for it I have found! I like to substitute canned chicken broth for the water and add a bit more ham.
This recipe comes from Gourmet Magazine,1995. 
Delicious!
keywords: Meat, Weeknight, Stove Top, < 4 Hours

recipeInstructions.text: In a large heavy kettle or stock pot cook bacon over moderate heat, stirring, until crisp and transfer to paper towels to drain.
Pour off all but about 1/4 cup bacon fat from kettle and cook onions and carrots, stirring, until softened.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer 2 hours uncovered, stirring occasionally and adding 1 to 2 cups more water (or broth) if soup becomes too thick.
Remove kettle from heat and transfer ham hock with a slotted spoon to a cutting board.
Discard fat and bones and chop meat.
Return meat to kettle and simmer soup, stirring, until heated through.
Discard bay leaf.
Just before serving, crumble bacon and sprinkle over soup.
Makes 8 cups.

name: Mushroom-Bacon Pasta
description: If you like mushrooms, you'll like this pasta dish! Make it a main course, or serve it as a side dish. As well, this dish easily doubles.
keywords: Pork, Vegetable, Meat, Canadian, Kid Friendly, < 30 Mins, Stove Top, Easy, Inexpensive

recipeInstructions.text: Note: use any type of mushrooms you like, or a combination; try button, cremini or shiitake.
Cook pasta according to package directions in a large pot of boiling salted water; cook until al dente then drain well; place in a serving bowl and reserve.
Meanwhile, in a large skillet over low heat, heat one tbsp of the olive oil.
Add bacon and mushrooms to skillet and cook, stirring, until browned.
Add remaining oil to skillet, then the capers, garlic, salt and hot pepper flakes.
Cook, stirring, for about 10 minutes or until garlic is just slightly golden.
Stir in basil (you can also substitute fresh parsley, for a different taste) and toss with cooked pasta.
Serve with parmesan cheese on the side.

name: Creamy Coleslaw For A Crowd
description: This is my grandmothers recipe. Everyone asks me to bring it for pot lucks. The trick was always the pickle juice. If you dont care for one of the vegetables just omit it and top up with another. This will serve 8 as a side salad.
keywords: Potluck, < 15 Mins, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Chop and mix all veggies in a medium size bowl.
Prepare dressing and stir into slaw.
Season to taste.
Best if left to sit overnight so juices drain into dressing but is still good the first day.

name: Mandarin Orange Cake With Pineapple Frosting
description: My aunt made this for Easter, and everyone loved it...no leftovers:(It is very simple and makes a nice presentation. I am not a big fan of mandarin oranges, but this cake is divine. I chop up the oranges just because I don't like big hunks of oranges, but you can leave them whole if you wish. A must try!! Baking time is approximate.
keywords: Pineapple, Tropical Fruits, Fruit, Low Protein, Kid Friendly, < 60 Mins, Oven, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Spray 9x13-inch baking pan with cooking spray.
Beat together all cake ingredients for 4 minutes.
Bake cake according to time on box.
Let cool completely.
Mix together all frosting ingredients.
Spread on cooled cake and refrigerate until serving.

name: Pork Chops With Asparagus And Mushrooms
description: This is a very easy dish to make. The mushrooms and asparagus really add to the flavor of the pork chops!
keywords: Pork, Vegetable, Meat, Very Low Carbs, < 60 Mins, Stove Top, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: In a skillet brown pork chops on both sides in olive oil (2-3 minutes).
Remove chops from skillet, keep warm.
Add white wine, garlic, onion, spices and worcestershire sauce to skillet, stir constantly.
Once onion and garlic are soft, add beef broth and place pork chops in skillet.
Cook on medium low for approximately 30 minutes covered.
Add asparagus and mushrooms, cover and cook 8-10 minutes.
Thicken sauce with cornstarch and serve over egg noodles or rice.
If you need more liquid, add more beef broth or wine to sauce.

name: Dusted Chocolate Pound Cake
description: Got this one from my sister Wendy. She made it for a family dinner and everyone went wild over it! Had to bring home the recipe!
keywords: Lunch/Snacks, Polish, European, Kid Friendly, Potluck, Christmas, Weeknight, Oven, < 4 Hours, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Heat oven to 325*; grease and flour bundt or tube pan.
Sift flour, cocoa, salt and baking powder together.
Beat shortening and butter together.
Slowly add sugar and beat until light and fluffy.
Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add flour mix and milk alternately to creamed mixture, beginning and ending with flour.
Add vanilla, mix well.
Pour into pan, place on center rack and bake 1-1/2 to 2 hours.
Check with wooden pick after 1-1/2 hours to see if it needs more time.

name: Apple Salad
description: This is my mom's recipe, it is quick & easy to make. tastes great as a salad or as dessert, color is very nice. Great for a large group, makes a huge bowl full.
keywords: Apple, Tropical Fruits, Fruit, Meat, Toddler Friendly, Kid Friendly, Sweet, St. Patrick's Day, Brunch, < 30 Mins, Refrigerator, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Put all ingredients in large bowl in order listed, stir well to blend.
Refrigerate until cold and serve.

name: Passover Cookies
description: These were the most amazing cookies I have every tasted. They are "very" crispy. I will make this year-round, not just for Passover.
keywords: Dessert, Cookie & Brownie, European, < 60 Mins

recipeInstructions.text: Mix together the first 7 ingredients.
Add the eggs and oil and mix together well.
The dough will seem dry and crumbly, but it will hold together when cooked.
Drop by tablespoons onto greased cookie sheet.  press lightly to hold together, if necessary.
Bake @ 350° for 15 minutes.

name: Roasted Asparagus
description: Make and share this Roasted Asparagus recipe from Food.com.
keywords: < 30 Mins, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the oil and garlic together and set aside to blend for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile: holding the asparagus in both hands, bend and they will snap off where they become tough.
Trim bottoms to even off.
Remove scales at the bottom.
Cut peppers in long slices.
Put asparagus in a zip-lock plastic bag and add the oil/garlic mix.
Toss to coat evenly.
Place asparagus on foil-lined baking sheet and roast in 450 degree oven for 5-10 minutes (depending on the size of the asparagus) till crisp-tender.
Remove from oven and add the peppers and toss to coat.
Return to oven for 5-10 minutes till peppers become crisp-tender.

name: Christmas Punch
description: Make and share this Christmas Punch recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Beverages, Pineapple, Tropical Fruits, Fruit, Low Protein, Low Cholesterol, Healthy, Christmas, < 15 Mins, No Cook, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Pour all of the juices together in a big punch bowl.
Add enough soda to give the punch a kick, but not so much that the flavor of the juices is diluted.

name: Best Popovers
description: Easy to make popovers are so good. These are so versatile.I use popovers for everything from tuna bisque to cream puffs.
keywords: Kid Friendly, < 60 Mins, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Mix all ingredients in large bowl.
Half fill greased muffin tins w/ mixture.
Put in cold oven and set temp to 450 degrees f.
Bake 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350 degrees f.
Bake for another 15-20 minutes.
Test one: make sure it is crispy outside and moist inside.

name: Silk And Satin Chocolate Pie
description: This is one of the dessert tray favourites at Captain Anderson's Restaurant and Waterfront Market, Panama City Beach, Florida.
keywords: Dessert, Fruit, Kid Friendly, Potluck, Christmas, Weeknight, No Cook, Refrigerator, < 4 Hours, Easy, Inexpensive

recipeInstructions.text: Cream butter and sugar until very light and fluffy.
In double boiler, melt chocolate and blend with vanilla.
Add the chilled eggs, one at a time, and beat with electric beater on medium speed for at least two minutes after adding each egg.
Pour into baked pie shell.
Chill at least three hours in refrigerator before serving.
Top with whipped cream or whipped topping and toasted almond slivers.

name: Boursin Cheese Potatoes
description: Not a "figure friendly" side dish, it tastes incredible. Nice to serve at special dinners or when you're not counting fat and calories.
keywords: Vegetable, Weeknight, < 4 Hours, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Slice potatoes into quarter inch rounds and toss with salt and pepper.
Slowly heat cream and cheese together until thoroughly melted.
In a deep casserole dish layer half the potatoes.
Cover with half the cream mixture.
Repeat.
Cover and bake at 350°f for one hour.
Sprinkle top with chives or parsley.

name: Uncle Bill S Soy-Ginger Marinade
description: This recipe not only tenderizes the meat but gives it a delightful taste, a very light touch of sweetness. Developed this recipe over 25 years ago. It is a must to try.
keywords: Uncle Bill S Soy-Ginger Marinade

recipeInstructions.text: In a mixing bowl, mix together all ingredients except beer; stir well.
Now add beer and stir gently so the marinade does not foam too much.
Prepare steaks,using a knife by scoring any fatty outside areas on steaks.
This prevents the steaks from curling.
Place steaks in a casserole dish.
Pour marinade over and using a fork, punch holes in the steaks so the marinade penetrates the steaks; punch both sides.
Cover and marinate for at least 4 hours in the refrigerator before cooking.
You may marinate for a longer period if desired.
This marinade is also excellent for roasts.
Barbecue or fry steaks to your desired doneness.
You can also substitute and use a dry red wine instead of beer.
Steaks should be about 1 inch in thickness.
Rib-eye steaks can be marinated for a different flavor, but i do not recommend as the rib eyes are good with some pepper and granulated garlic powder.
If you are using chuck steaks, i suggest that you marinate for at least 24 hours or longer.
This marinade is excellent to marinate roast beef of your choice.

name: Creamy Bacon-Ranch Pasta Salad
description: Simple flavors are quick and tasty. Nice change if your tired of making or bringing potato or green salads! Warning: you will be asked to make it again and again.
keywords: Refrigerator

recipeInstructions.text: Mix mayo and ranch seasoning until well blended.
Set aside.
In large bowl combine pasta, tomatos, cucumbers, and mayo mixture.
Add salt, pepper, and bacon bits.
Let pasta salad set 4-6 hours or overnight if possible.
Add more mayo if needed before serving (the creamier the better!).
Serve chilled.
My husband is a cheese lover and likes me to add 2 cups of shredded sharp cheddar.
For a change of color, i use garden blend spiral pasta.

name: Garden Tuna Melts
description: Got this great recipe from Kraft. My whole family loves this, especially my DH. Very easy and quick for those busy days.
keywords: Tuna, Cheese, < 30 Mins, Stove Top, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Mix tuna, mayo, onion, green pepper, and seasonings.
Cover each of 4 bread slices with tuna mixture, one slice of cheese and second bread slice; spread outsides of sandwiches with butter.
Cook in skillet on medium heat until lightly browned on both sides and cheese is melted.

name: Zucchini Cake
description: Make and share this Zucchini Cake recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Lunch/Snacks, Grains, Fruit, Nuts, European, Kid Friendly, Potluck, < 60 Mins, For Large Groups, Oven, Easy, Inexpensive

recipeInstructions.text: Mix dry ingredients.
Combine oil and eggs with vanilla; add to dry ingredients, mix well.
Add zucchini, stir until combined well.
Fold in walnuts.
Place in greased 13x9 baking pan.
Bake at 350* for 40 minutes, or until pick comes out clean.

name: Seared Steak Pepper Onion Fajitas From Fine Cooking
description: Great weeknight recipe! Goes together quickly and is easy and delicious. I love the crust my cast-iron skillet provides. Sometimes I use Penzey's Southwest seaoning in place of the cumin mixture.
keywords: Tex Mex, Southwestern U.S., Mexican, < 30 Mins, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Combine the salt, pepper, cumin and cayenne in a small bowl.
Rub the steak with the seasoning on both sides.
Heat the oil in a 10-inch heavy skillet (preferably cast iron) over medium-high heat until very hot but not smoking.
Put the steak in the hot pan and sear for 3 minutes.
Turn the steak and cook for another 2 minutes (it will be very rare but will cook more later on).
Take the skillet off the heat, transfer the steak to a cutting board, and cover loosely with foil.
Return the skillet to medium heat.
Add the pepper and onion slices and sauté, stirring frequently, until soft, about 8 min.
Add the jalapeno and garlic and cook until soft and fragrant, about 1 min.
Slide the skillet off the heat and stir in the lime juice, scraping up any browned bits from the pan.
Cover to keep warm.
Trim the fat from the side of the steak and cut the steak into thin (1/8- to 1/4-inch) slices.
Add the slices to the skillet along with any accumulated juices.
Toss until well blended.
Stir in the chopped cilantro and season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately with warm flour tortillas, sliced avocado, sour cream, chopped tomatoes, and cilantro sprigs.

name: Batter For Sweet And Sour Shrimp
description: Make and share this Batter for Sweet and Sour Shrimp recipe from Food.com.
keywords: < 30 Mins, For Large Groups, Deep Fried, Easy, Inexpensive

recipeInstructions.text: Mix together and let set for 10 minutes.
Dip shrimp in batter and shake off excess.
Deep fry 350 degree f for 5-6 minutes.
Drain on paper towels.
Keep warm in 200 degree f oven until ready to serve.

name: Caramel Frosted Apple Cake
description: A moist cake that really goes fast at the family gatherings. It's a great one to take on camping trips too!
keywords: Lunch/Snacks, Apple, Fruit, German, Polish, European, Kid Friendly, Potluck, Weeknight, Oven, < 4 Hours, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Mix oil and sugars.
Add eggs, 1 at a time, beat well after each.
Mix dry ingredients, add to batter and mix well.
Fold in apples, walnuts, vanilla.
Pour into greased and floured tube pan.
Bake at 325* for 1-1/2 hr, or until cake tests done.
Cool.
Frosting: heat on low, brown sugar, cream, butter and salt until sugar is dissolved.
Cool to room temperature.
Beat in the powdered sugar until smooth.
Drizzle over cake.

name: Mashed Potatoes With Ham
description: My Polish grandmother could work magic with a few simple ingredients. A refreshing change from the the complex and highly seasoned foods of modern cuisine.
keywords: Pork, Potato, Vegetable, Meat, Polish, European, Kid Friendly, < 60 Mins, Oven, Easy, Inexpensive

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°f.
Beat egg yolks with mashed potatoes and season with salt and pepper.
Add sour cream and ham.
Beat egg whites until stiff and fold into potato mixture.
Place in a buttered casserole, dot with butter and bake 30 minutes.

name: Baked Ziti
description: Make and share this Baked Ziti recipe from Food.com.
keywords: European, Kid Friendly, < 60 Mins, Oven

recipeInstructions.text: Chop onion into fine small pieces and brown with ground beef.
Sprinkle garic salt on.
Drain.
Add ziti and spaghetti sauce and mix well.
Spoon into a greased 9*13 in pan.
Top with cheese.
Cover and bake at 350.
I also like to add a can of mushrooms.

name: Julie S Perfect Potato Salad
description: My family would crowd into the kitchen to get their first forkfull of Mom's potato salad. It's that good! This potato salad is not at all sweet - something which was important for our family. Let it sit in the fridge as long as you can before serving... it's even better the next day!
keywords: Vegetable, Kid Friendly, Potluck, Thanksgiving, < 15 Mins

recipeInstructions.text: Steam potatoes with skin on.
Mix together all ingredients except potatoes.
When potatoes are done, cut (it's up to you whether or not you want to leave the skins on) while still warm and fold together with the mayo mixture - it makes it taste better to combine while warm.
Put into serving container and garnish.
Refrigerate for at least three hours before serving (the longer the better).
This potato salad is even better then next day!
Note from julie: i use the dried minced onion because i like their texture, omit the celery, and add about 1/4 tsp of both curry powder and dried mustard... but don't tell mom.  ;)

name: Tuna Brown Rice Salad
description: I adapted this recipe from one I found in a cookbook. It is not only healthy, it is delicious! Perfect to take to the office for lunch, or just to snack on at home with crackers.
keywords: Brown Rice, Rice, Low Cholesterol, Healthy, < 60 Mins, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Mix relish, vinegar, oil and mustard.
Add remaining ingredients and toss to coat.
Allow to marinate in the refrigerator at least 15 minutes before serving.

name: Oven Baked Crab Cakes
description: Make and share this Oven Baked Crab Cakes recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Potluck, < 60 Mins, Oven, Refrigerator, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Spread crushed cornflakes in a shallow baking pan.
Whisk mayonnaise, mustard, seasoning, cayenne and egg yolk.
Add crab meat.
S& p to taste.
Divide crab cake mixture into 10 equal piles and form slightly flattened cakes.
Turn cakes over in crushed corn flakes until covered.
Cover pan w/ plastic, transfer cakes to pan and cover with more plastic wrap.
Chill 2-4 hours.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees f.
Transfer crab cakes to a large greased baking sheet.
Put about 1/2 teaspoon butter on each crab cake.
Bake around 15 minutes.
Cakes should be golden brown.

name: Garden Herb Bread
description: You are going to love this bread. It smells so good while its cooking. Sort of like turkey stuffing. It is great used as such as well. Nothing like creating your own bread cubes for your holiday turkey or fresh croutons for a summer salad. Try this bread with any cold meat sandwich for a pleasent suprise. Use dried herbs that are flaked and not ground. If using ground, reduce the amount by half. If using fresh herbs, double the amount.
keywords: Breads, Grains, Healthy, Weeknight, Bread Machine, Small Appliance, < 4 Hours, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Load ingredients into your machine in the order given.
Bake using the regular, rapid, or delayed time bake cycle.

name: Pot Roast
description: Make and share this Pot Roast recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Vegetable, Meat, German, European, Kid Friendly, Weeknight, Stove Top, Easy, Inexpensive

recipeInstructions.text: In dutch oven, brown roast in oil.
Add onions and saute briefly.
Add broth; cover and cook on low for 2 hours;,add more broth if necessary.
Add all other ingredients.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and cook for 1-1/2 hours more.

name: Vegetable And Ground Beef Soup
description: Make and share this Vegetable and Ground Beef Soup recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Low Cholesterol, Healthy, Weeknight, < 4 Hours

recipeInstructions.text: Sauté beef in pot or skillet until browned.
Add the beef, onion, cabbage and water in a large pot and boil until cabbage is tender.
Add the rest of the ingredients.
Add water till you have 2 inches of water above the solid part of soup.
Bring to a boil and then turn heat down and simmer about 45 minutes.

name: Borden S Mini Cheesecakes
description:
These are festive little cakes After cooled garnish with a sprinkle of cake sprinkles or get creative and use fresh berries; fresh sliced fruits; toasted coconut..... Prep time unknown; baking time 20 minutes
THE BORDEN'S EAGLE BRAND CONDENSED MILK PROVIDES THE SWEETNESS TO THE CHEESECAKE MIXTURE...SUGAR IS NOT NEEDED. (except for stated amount in crust.)
keywords: Dessert, Cheese, Potluck, < 30 Mins, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 300 degrees f.
Line cupcake tin with cupcake papers (24).
Combine crumbs, sugar and butter; press equal portions onto bottom of cupcake papers.
In large mixing bowl beat cheese until fluffy.
Gradually beat in condensed milk until smooth.
Add eggs and vanilla; mix well.
Spoon equal amounts into prepared cups (about 3 tbl per cup).
Bake 20 minutes or until cakes spring back when touched lightly.
Cool and chill.
Garnish with fresh berries or sliced fruits; chocolate shavings; toasted coconut; or cake sprinkles for a festive look.

name: Chicken And Cheese French Bread Pizza
description: Make and share this Chicken and Cheese French Bread Pizza recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Poultry, Meat, Kid Friendly, < 30 Mins, Oven

recipeInstructions.text: Combine first 5 ingredients in a small bowl, and spread evenly over bread slices.
Mix together chicken, salt, and pepper.
Spread chicken evenly over bread slices; sprinkle with mozzarella cheese, bell pepper, and green onion.
Bake at 350 degrees for 10 minutes or until cheese melts.

name: Oatmeal Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Make and share this Oatmeal Peanut Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Dessert, Cookie & Brownie, Kid Friendly, < 60 Mins, For Large Groups, Oven

recipeInstructions.text: Beat butter and peanut butter at medium speed with an electric mixer until fluffy; gradually add sugar and brown sugar, beating well.
Add eggs and vanilla; mixing well.
Combine oats and baking soda; add to butter mixture, mixing well.
Stir in morsels; drop by tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350° degrees for 9-10 minutes.
Cool on cookie sheets 5 minutes; remove to wire racks to cool completely.

name: Ham Roll-Ups
description: I am usually being hovered over when I make these, so they never make it past "roll'er up". These are so yummy and can be very low cal depending on the type and amount of cream cheese used.
keywords: Ham, Pork, Cheese, Meat, Very Low Carbs, Low Protein, Low Cholesterol, Kid Friendly, Spring, Summer, Winter, < 15 Mins, No Cook, Beginner Cook, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Take two pieces of ham and overlap them so that the top slice is halfway onto the bottom slice.
Spread the whole thing with cream cheese as thick or thin as you like (and no need to get it perfect). place a pickle spear at the end of the bottom ham slice and roll'er up!
If this is just for you, have at it.
Or if you're sharing, roll up as many as you'd like and place in the freezer for 5 to 10 minutes to make them easy to slice.
Slice into thick pieces, then spear with toothpicks if you'd like.

name: Spaghetti And Italian Meatballs
description: This is one of my families favorites, as it was mine when I was a kid. Of course it always tastes better the second day. The bread in the meatballs gives them a wonderful texture and flavor.
keywords: Meat, Low Cholesterol, Weeknight, < 4 Hours

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the onion in hot oil until it is tender but not brown.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, sugar, salt, pepper, oregano and bay leaves.
Simmer for 30 minutes.  as the sauce simmers keep an eye on it, if it looks too thick add some water up to one cup.
While the sauce is simmering mix together the meatballs.
To dry the bread i preheat my oven to it's lowest setting (170 degrees) and when it gets to temp i turn it off and place the bread slices in and let the low heat dry them.
Remove from the oven and place in a mixing bowl.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees and line a cookie sheet with sides with foil.
Soak the dried bread in water 2-3 mintues, then squeeze out the moisture.
(doing this does something to the gluten in the bread that gives the meatballs a wonderful taste and texture).
Combine the bread with the rest of the ingredients, mixing well with your hands.
Form into small balls (approx 20).
Bake for 15 minutes or until they are cooked through.
Remove from the pan and add to the simmering sauce.
Cook for 30 minutes longer.
Serve over hot spaghetti noodles.

name: Dijon Broccoli
description: Make and share this Dijon Broccoli recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Grains, Vegetable, Canadian, European, Spicy, Christmas, Thanksgiving, < 30 Mins, Steam, Stove Top, Easy, Inexpensive

recipeInstructions.text: Steam the broccoli until it is barely tender.
Combine all other ingredients and heat until butter melts.
Stir to blend.
Pour over the hot broccoli.

name: Lucy Belle S Funky Chicken Casserole
description: This is a recipe from a book My Aunt Debbie gave me. The Treasury of White Trash Cooking. It does not say what size casserole dish to use. Or How many servings it makes. You decide.
keywords: Chicken, Poultry, Cheese, Meat, Potluck, Weeknight, Oven, Beginner Cook, < 4 Hours, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the stuffing mix, water, and butter together.
Put half of the mix into a casserole dish.
Now, mix the chicken, onion, celery, and mayonnaise together.
Sprinkle with salt and pour it in the dish, on top of the bread mixture.
Now combine the rest of the stuffing mixture with the eggs and milk and pour on top.
Refrigerate overnight.
Take out casserole 1 hour before baking and spread chicken soup over the top.
Bake this uncovered at 350 for 40 minutes.
Now, remove the casserole from the oven and coat the top heavily with your grated cheese.
Put it bake in the oven for another 10 minutes, or until the cheese melts.

name: Low Fat Oat Bran Apricot Muffins
description: Make and share this Low Fat Oat Bran Apricot Muffins recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Breads, < 30 Mins, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven 425 degrees f.
Spray muffin tins with pan-spray.
(these tend to stick to paper cup cake liners).
Mix first 4 ingredients; set aside.
Mix egg substitute, juice, milk and oil; add fruit and mix into dry ingredients till just moistened.
Pour into prepared muffin tins.
Bake 15-17 minutes.

name: Moussaka
description: Make and share this Moussaka recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Cheese, Meat, Greek, European, Weeknight, Oven, < 4 Hours

recipeInstructions.text: Brown eggplant slices in olive oil (or, spray with olive oil and bake@350* for 10-12 minutes).
Heat 4 tbs oil and cook onions and garlic until golden.
Add browned lamb and cook together to blend flavors.
Combine wine, tomato paste, cinnamon, parsley, salt and pepper.
Stir into meat and simmer, stirring frequently until all the liquid is absorbed.
Preheat oven to 375°f prepare topping.
Melt butter, add flour mixing well.
Add hot milk, stirring constantly until thick and smooth.
Remove from heat, cool slightly, stir in beaten egg, nutmeg and ricotta.
Grease a casserole dish and sprinkle the bottom with bread crumbs.
Arrange alternate layers of eggplant and meat mixture, sprinkling each layer with bread crumbs and grated parmesan.
Top with the cheese custard.
Bake 1 hour or until top is puffy and golden brown.
Cool 20-30 minutes before serving.
Serves 8.
This can be frozen uncooked.

name: Roasted Caraway Potatoes
description: Make and share this Roasted Caraway Potatoes recipe from Food.com.
keywords: Vegetable, Low Protein, Low Cholesterol, Healthy, Weeknight, < 4 Hours

recipeInstructions.text: Combine first 2 ingredients in a large heavy duty zip-top plastic bag.
Mix together remaining ingredients and pour into plastic bag.
Shake well to coat.
Place potato mixture in an ungreased 13x9 inch pan.
Bake at 400 degrees for 1 hour or until potatoes are tender, stirring occasionally.

name: Great Balls Of Fire
description: Make and share this Great Balls of Fire recipe from Food.com.
keywords: High In..., < 60 Mins, Oven, Easy

recipeInstructions.text: Mix all ingredients thoroughly.
Roll tablespoonful of mixture into balls.
Place on cookie sheet and bake at 350 degrees for 10 minutes.
Turn balls over and bake 10 minutes more or until done.

name: Tuna Ring With Cheese Sauce
description: This is from my mother's Betty Crocker Recipe Card Library from the 70's. I've been enjoying it for 3 decades! It's so delicious, and not as hard as the recipe is lengthy. It makes even a novice cook look pretty darn impressive!
keywords: Kid Friendly, < 60 Mins, Oven, Inexpensive

recipeInstructions.text: Filling: beat egg slightly; set aside 2 t egg.
Stir tuna, onion, cheese, parsley, celery salt, and pepper into remaining egg.
(you can do this part ahead and keep in refrigerator until ready to use.) dough: stir baking mix& water to a soft dough.
Knead 5 times on a floured cloth covered board.
(i just do this on a floured surface.) roll out into a rectangle.
Spread with filling.
Roll up to make a long roll.
Place sealed edge down on greased baking sheet.
(i make a circle or a half-circle.) with scissors, make cuts 2/3 deep at 1
Intervals.
(i slightly turn each piece to show filling.) brush top with reserved egg.
Bake at 375f for 25-30 minutes.
Meanwhile, make cheese sauce.
Cheese sauce: melt butter over low heat.
Blend in baking mix, salt, and pepper.
Cook over low heat, stirring, until smooth and bubbly.
Remove from heat.
Stir in milk.
Heat to boiling, stirring constantly.
Boil and stir one minute.
Stir in cheese until melted.

(i rarely bring this to a boil. i just make sure it's nice and hot, bringing the heat up slowly. maybe it's my own quirk, but i don't scorch the milk that way. i slice the tuna ring and serve the slices and pass the cheese sauce. this is so yummy!).

name: Farmer S Breakfast
